title: Model Size and Small Countermodels
quickIdea: The quantifier prefix decides how large a model needs to be: every existential needs a witness, and a universal that held over a big domain still holds over the part you keep.
remember: If a sentence with k leading existentials and no function symbols has a model at all, it has one with at most k elements.
Reason: keep only the elements that witness the leading existentials. A universal that was true over the whole domain stays true over a subset of it.
Function symbols break the argument, because deleting an element can leave f(a) with no value; that is why the question states that no function symbols occur.
A given model size is never forced: a sentence with a 7-element model may also have models of size 1, 3 or 100.
To refute a sentence, a domain of two elements is usually enough; a single countermodel is enough to deny validity.

Concrete example: there exists s there exists t there exists u for all v psi(s, t, u, v) with a 7-element model also has a model of size at most 3, and possibly of size 1 if the three witnesses coincide.

example.prompt: The sentence there exists s there exists t there exists u for all v psi(s, t, u, v) has a model with a 7-element universe. Must it have a model with at most 3 elements?
example.work: In the 7-element model take the three witnesses s, t, u and drop the other four elements. The universal now ranges over a subset, and a universal true on a set is true on any subset.
example.answer: Yes - a model of size at most 3 always exists. It may be smaller still if two witnesses are the same element.

gateAngle: This is GATE CS 2018 Q.28: three leading existentials and no function symbols force a model of size at most three, and the other options claim things the hypotheses never guarantee, such as no small model or a forced size of exactly seven.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: See GATE CS 2018 Q.28 in the linked PYQs.
variations.answer: Option (A): there exists a model with universe of size at most 3.
variations.why: Keep the three existential witnesses; the universal part is inherited by the subset.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: There exists x for all y R(x, y) has a model of size 5. Is there a model of size 1?
variations.why: Keep only the witness x. The universal then ranges over {x} alone, and R(x, x) already holds in the 5-element model.

trap.what: Reading the given model size as a bound in both directions.
trap.why: The hypothesis says a model of that size exists; it says nothing about models of other sizes unless the prefix forces a bound.
trap.counterexample: There exists x for all y R(x, y) has models of size 1, 2, 5 and 100 at once, by taking R to be the full relation on each domain.

check.question: A sentence has prefix there exists x there exists y for all z. Its smallest model has how many elements at most?
check.explanation: Two existential witnesses are needed, so a model with at most two elements exists whenever any model exists, provided no function symbols occur.
